subject: Onboarding validation playbook + evidence package for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding validation playbook + evidence package for Acme Retail

Hi Daniel —

Following our kickoff yesterday, attaching the onboarding validation playbook we plan to use for the Acme integration. The goal for the first run is to validate throughput and tail latency at your peak QPS, collect ramp evidence, and confirm fallback behavior for model/region failover.

High-level asks from Acme for the week of Nov 30:
- Confirm target steady-state QPS (you mentioned ~350 QPS with 512-token avg payload)
- Provide representative sample payloads and percentiles for payload sizes (light/median/heavy)
- Confirm whether inference traffic originates from a single VPC region or multiple regions

Attached: redwood_onboard_validation_playbook_v1.xlsx — includes the test matrix, ramp schedule, success criteria, and artifact list.

Proposed test window: Dec 2, 09:00–13:00 PT. If that works, Rishi will run the pre-flight tooling one business day prior to confirm environment connectivity and model variant selection.

Quick next steps:
1) Reply with sample payloads (or drop in the Drive link).
2) Confirm the stated QPS and preferred test window.
3) We’ll enumerate any ACL/IP allowlist entries needed for the load agents.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20m prep call if helpful.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the playbook and the clear checklist. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the window: 

1) QPS: We validated internal traffic and can commit to a 380 QPS steady-state for the demo (peak bursts up to ~520 QPS for 2–3 minutes).
2) Payloads: I’ll attach a small set of representative payloads and a spreadsheet with size percentiles (light: 64 tokens, median: 320 tokens, heavy: 1024 tokens).
3) Region: Traffic originates from our us-west-2 VPC only for now.

Security note: Our security team requested the list of outbound IPs your load agents will use and whether the test harness stores logs longer than 7 days. We need that before the pre-flight.

I’m fine with the Dec 2 window but can shift to Dec 3 if you need more prep time.

Thanks,
Daniel

Subject: Re: Onboarding validation playbook + evidence package for Acme Retail

Thanks Daniel — good detail. I pulled the playbook and sketched a condensed technical checklist for the pre-flight and test run:

Pre-flight (Day -1)
- Connectivity: verify agent -> Redwood control-plane TLS and allowlist (we will provide the agent IP block)
- Model variant: confirm which model and quantization profile you want pinned for the run (we can run 13B-quant or 70B-fp depending on cost/latency tradeoff)
- KV/prefix caching: confirm if your app will warm prefixes or if tests should exercise cold-starts

Ramp & steady-state test (Day 0)
- Ramp 0 -> 100 qps in 5m, 100 -> 250 qps in next 10m, 250 -> 380 qps in 10m; hold steady for 20m
- Inject 3 burst events to 520 qps for 2–3m each at minutes 40, 65, 90
- Collect: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (token-level and request-level), CPU/GPU utilization, batching efficiency, and dropped/failed request counts
- Success criteria: p95 request latency < 450ms and no more than 0.2% failed requests during steady-state

Artifact capture & evidence exchange
- We will produce a compressed evidence bundle (ramp CSV, server telemetry, agent logs, failed request samples) and upload to the Drive link within 24h of run completion
- Please include a sample of your top-10 worst-case payloads in acme_sample_payloads.json so we can reproduce any heavy tail behavior

Security/retention notes
- Agent logs are retained 7 days by default; if you need shorter retention we can enable ephemeral mode for the test (logs retained 24 hours)
- Outbound agent IP range: 34.201.12.0/24 (we will provide the final list once agents are scheduled)

Let me know which model variant to pin and whether to enable prefix warmup before the run — I can schedule the pre-flight for Dec 1 afternoon PT.

— Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Rishi/Monica — thanks, this is great and very actionable. A couple of answers: 

- Model: Start with the 13B-quant profile for the run (cost conscious, we want to validate latency first). If results look good we’ll test 70B-fp on a follow-up run.
- Prefix warmup: yes — we can seed the top 50 prefixes; please include warmup in the pre-flight.
- Security: 7-day retention is fine for now; thanks for the outbound IP range. I’ll ask our infra team to allowlist 34.201.12.0/24 and confirm once complete.

I’ll also drop a Drive link with the payloads and a small readme describing traffic patterns.

Can we keep Dec 2 as the test date? The 09:00–13:00 PT window works for our infra team.

Best,
Daniel

- Model variant: 13B-quant (warm prefixes seeded)
- QPS: steady-state 380 QPS, bursts to 520 QPS (as planned)
- Retention: default 7 days for agent logs

I’ll send a calendar invite for a 20m pre-flight sync on Dec 1 at 14:00 PT (invite includes the Drive link). If anything changes, reply-all and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
